description: Governance-manager integration: wire GovernanceEngine into ContextManager so all governance-gated operations are exclusively routed through the engine with no bypass. Covers engine storage, CM method exposure, action variant expansion, execution wiring, timeout/deadlock handling, conflict resolution, checkpoint cosignatures, and integration testing.

stories.title: Store GovernanceEngine in PerContextState and construct in builder
stories.description:
Add a `governance_engine: Mutex<Box<dyn GovernanceEngine>>` field to `PerContextState` in manager.rs. The engine is wrapped in its own Mutex (separate from the global `contexts: Mutex<HashMap>`) so governance operations do not hold the global lock during engine calls.

Two type systems coexist by design: `GovernanceModel` (simple variant-only enum in params.rs, derives Eq, lives in ContextParams) selects which model; `GovernanceModelConfig` (rich enum with data in governance/mod.rs) configures the engine. Currently `GovernanceModel` only has `SingleAdmin` — expand it to have all four variants (SingleAdmin, Threshold, Majority, Unanimity) matching GovernanceModelConfig. The builder maps `GovernanceModel` + creation arguments (creator_did, signers, threshold, etc.) to the appropriate `GovernanceModelConfig` and constructs the engine.

Also change `GovernanceModelConfig::Majority.min_participation` from `f64` to `u32` basis points (e.g., 5000 = 50%) so GovernanceModelConfig can derive `Eq`.

Replace the builder.rs governance validation placeholder comment ('ContextParams always has a governance field, so this is a placeholder for future governance model validation') with actual engine construction and validation logic.

At creation time, mint `GovernancePropose` and `GovernanceVote` UCAN tokens for designated voters per ADR-031 §6: Threshold signers each receive both; Majority/Unanimity members with GovernanceVote role capability receive them at role assignment.

The engine is immutable for the context's lifetime (per ADR-031 §4). Re-export `GovernanceModelConfig` from context/mod.rs if not already exported.

stories.title: Expose propose/approve/reject/withdraw on ContextManager
stories.description:
Add public methods on ContextManager that delegate to the stored GovernanceEngine: `propose_governance_action()`, `approve_governance_proposal()`, `reject_governance_proposal()`, `withdraw_governance_vote()`. Each method acquires the global contexts lock briefly to get the PerContextState reference, then acquires the per-engine Mutex<Box<dyn GovernanceEngine>> lock for engine delegation. This two-lock approach prevents the global lock from being held during engine operations.

Each method constructs a GovernanceContext snapshot from PerContextState, delegates to the engine's corresponding method, and records governance events in the event log. The propose method validates that the proposer holds `GovernancePropose` capability (UCAN). The approve/reject methods validate that the voter holds `GovernanceVote` capability.

Signing key plumbing: propose, approve, and reject methods accept a `signing_key: &ed25519_dalek::SigningKey` parameter (required by the GovernanceEngine trait for Ed25519 vote signatures). withdraw_governance_vote does NOT take a signing key (per the trait definition — withdrawal is the voter's privileged operation on their own vote).

Return types: propose_governance_action returns `ProposalOutcome { proposal: GovernanceProposal, status: ProposalStatus, execution_result: Option<GovernanceActionResult> }`. The execution_result field is always None in this story — it exists so SCP-270 can populate it when auto-execution is wired without changing the struct. approve/reject/withdraw return `Result<ProposalStatus, ContextError>`.

Per ADR-031 §4a, SingleAdmin.propose() simultaneously creates and approves (status = Approved). Per sketch.md §6, these are the three-method mandatory protocol contract.

Auto-execution (calling execute_governance_action when status becomes Approved and populating execution_result) is NOT wired in this story — that is SCP-270's responsibility where the action dispatch lives.

stories.title: Wire all GovernanceAction variants through execute_governance_action with auto-execution
stories.description:
Extend `execute_governance_action()` to handle all 19 GovernanceAction variants. For each variant, implement the internal execution method. The catch-all arm that returns PermissionDenied('not yet supported') must be replaced with actual dispatch for every variant.

Wire auto-execution: when the GovernanceEngine returns Approved status (from propose for SingleAdmin, from approve/reject for multi-admin models), ContextManager automatically calls execute_governance_action(). This was moved from SCP-268 to this story because action dispatch lives here.

Remove or restrict any standalone public methods that bypass governance. All governed actions MUST be exclusively available through GovernanceEngine — the engine cannot be circumvented. Specifically: close_context() for multi-admin models must route through governance (propose -> vote -> execute). SingleAdmin close_context() still works via auto-approve but goes through the engine.

Protocol-level unanimity overrides (enforced by ContextManager, not the engine): ExtendTtl and PromoteContext always require unanimous consent from ALL current members regardless of governance model, per spec §5.10 and ADR-031 §4d.

UCAN updates on signer changes per ADR-031 §6: AddSigner execution mints GovernanceVote + GovernancePropose UCANs for the new signer. RemoveSigner execution revokes governance UCANs and validates threshold <= remaining signers.len().

Governance actions that result in membership changes (AddMember, RemoveMember) trigger MLS operations per ADR-031 §8: AddMember triggers MLS add_member() Commit, RemoveMember triggers MLS remove_member() Commit. The sequence is: proposal approved -> ContextManager executes membership change -> MLS Commit advances epoch -> GovernanceActionExecuted event appended.

stories.title: Implement governance proposal timeout task with deadlock detection
stories.description:
Implement the GovernanceTimeoutTask specified in ADR-031 §5. The SDK runs a background task that checks active proposals every 60 seconds. When a proposal's voting_deadline passes without resolution, the task calls resolve() which transitions the proposal to Expired or Rejected (model-specific rules per ADR-031 §4b-4d). The timeout task uses the per-engine Mutex (from SCP-267) — it acquires the global contexts lock briefly to get the PerContextState reference, then acquires the per-engine lock for resolve() calls.

The timeout task also handles per ADR-031 §5: proposer departure (Pending -> Invalidated), voter departure (vote removed, quorum recalculated), and epoch reset (votes invalidated per ADR-029 Tier 3 — group state reset changes the member's epoch context).

Deadlock detection and recovery per ADR-031 §10: The task detects deadlock conditions: Threshold (fewer than threshold signers active), Majority (fewer than ceil(eligible_voters * min_participation_bps / 10000) responsive over 3 consecutive windows), Unanimity (eligible voter offline beyond Tier 3 threshold of 7+ days). On deadlock detection, any member with GovernancePropose capability can propose a ReconfigureGovernance meta-action. The recovery uses fallback quorum: majority-of-active, regardless of original model. Requires >= 2 active voters. Recovery proposals have 48-hour voting window (double default). Model TYPE never changes. Logged as GovernanceDeadlockRecovery event.

The task runs per-context and is started when the context enters Active state. It stops when the context is closed.

stories.title: Implement governance conflict detection and resolution
stories.description:
Implement the governance conflict resolution protocol specified in ADR-031 §7. Conflicts arise when two approved proposals in the event log are incompatible: mutual RemoveMember (targeting each other's proposers), competing ChangeRole (same DID, different roles), competing ModifyCeiling (different ceiling sets), or RemoveMember + ChangeRole for the same DID.

Sequential conflicts (different event log sequence numbers): the proposal with the lower sequence number wins. The loser becomes Invalidated with reason 'Conflicting proposal {winner_id} committed first'. A GovernanceConflict event is appended.

Simultaneous conflicts (same sequence number, extremely rare): the context is frozen for new governance actions (no new proposals accepted). Message sending and tool invocation continue normally. A GovernanceConflictDetected event is emitted. Resolution requires an explicit ResolveConflict governance action from any DID with GovernanceVote capability. The resolution specifies AcceptProposal { winner_id } or InvalidateBoth. The ResolveConflict action itself follows the context's governance model. If no resolution is reached within the voting window (48 hours), both proposals are invalidated and the freeze is lifted.

stories.title: Implement governance-aware checkpoint cosignatures
stories.description:
Implement model-specific checkpoint cosignature requirements per ADR-031 §9. The checkpointing system must know the governance model to determine the signature quorum for checkpoint attestation.

SingleAdmin: only the admin signs checkpoints; cosignatures field is empty. Threshold: checkpoints require threshold signatures from the signer set. The checkpoint creator distributes the checkpoint hash to other signers, who verify and cosign. Majority: checkpoints require signatures from >50% of eligible voters. Unanimity: checkpoints require signatures from all eligible voters.

Cosignature collection follows the same voting-window pattern as governance proposals but with a shorter default window of 1 hour. If cosignature quorum is not reached within the window, the checkpoint is still valid with the creator's signature alone but is flagged as PartiallyAttested — members can decide how much weight to give it.

This depends on SCP-267 (governance model must be available in PerContextState) but is otherwise independent of the governance method exposure and action wiring stories.
